# The expected files

What a given subcommand must write for a given input, byte for byte. An
end-to-end test compares them with the program's output through `MatchesFile`
(`src/test/e2e/cli/cli_run.hpp`), which reports the first line that differs. Issue
[#543](https://github.com/Guyot-Bertrand/sub-edit/issues/543).

**An expected file is never generated by the program under test.** A file the tool
wrote and a test then reads back proves only that the tool agrees with itself
(lesson of [#338](https://github.com/Guyot-Bertrand/sub-edit/issues/338)). Each
file below says where it comes from.

| File | Input | Provenance |
| :------ | :----- | :--------- |
| `mentions.hearing-impaired.srt` | `valides/mentions.srt`, subcommand `hearing-impaired` | **written by hand**, from the input and the removal rule: mentions in square brackets and parentheses go, a subtitle they empty disappears and the following ones are renumbered, a numeric reference `[1]` stays, a dialogue dash left alone goes, a mention split by the line break takes with it the space around it and leaves two lines. The real output was used only to check this expected file, never to copy it. |

## `json/` — the output of `--format json`

One `.jsonl` file per case, **written by hand**, from what ADR 0038 says about the
shape and what the input contains: one object per input, in order, the envelope, the
counts each subcommand declares. The end-to-end test (`json_test.cpp`) compares them
with the standard output through `MatchesFile`, **after replacing the test's temporary
directory with `<scratch>` and the corpus directory with `<corpus>`** — they change from
one run and one machine to the next, and an expected file that contained them would be
true nowhere. `src/scripts/check-json-fixtures.py` rereads them with a parser that is not
ours: valid JSON, envelope, no number with a decimal point.

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `json/inspect-batch.jsonl` | `inspect` on a readable file, a missing one and an unreadable one | written by hand; the real output was used only to check |
| `json/inspect-grid.jsonl` | `inspect` on `grilles/grille-24-courte.srt` and on a file counted in frames | by hand, from the table in `grilles/LISEZMOI.md` (24 frames/s, span of 10 s, two rates not separated); `concentration_permille` read from the measurement, 99.9 % |
| `json/shift-batch.jsonl` | `shift` on three inputs, the second of which is unreadable | by hand: "never zero, never two" |
| `json/writers.jsonl` | `transform`, `framerate`, `snap`, `hearing-impaired`, `convert` on the same file | by hand: the counts each declares, all zero except the subtitles |
| `json/warnings.jsonl` | a SubRip file without numbering, at each narration level | by hand: one `missing-numbering` diagnostic per block, `settled` since the reading numbered them |
| `json/adjust.jsonl` | `adjust` on a four-subtitle file, thirteen settings (defaults, `off`, `--shorten`, `--maximum`, `--gap`, `--range`…) | **by hand**, from Gaupol's order (speed, minimum, maximum, gap — the gap wins): each end and each count was worked out on paper before being compared; `constraints` says the settings used. The input file and the expected ends are in `src/test/e2e/cli/adjust_test.cpp` |
| `json/recoupement-defaut.jsonl`, `json/recoupement-ecart.jsonl` | `adjust --dry-run --maximum 6` (and `--gap 0.5`) on the nine files of `durees/` | **by hand**, from the definitions of the room and the need — see `durees/LISEZMOI.md`; the measuring script is checked against the same lines |
| `json/dry-run-writers.jsonl` | the six subcommands that write, with `--dry-run` and no destination | by hand: `dry_run` true, `destination` null, the counts of `writers.jsonl`; `changes` empty for `hearing-impaired`, which lists its changes |
| `json/dry-run-hearing-impaired.jsonl` | `hearing-impaired --dry-run` on `valides/mentions.srt` | by hand, from the input and the rule (see `mentions.hearing-impaired.srt`): subtitles 1 (removed, `after` null), 2, 4 and 5 change, numbered as in the file read; the 3rd, a reference, stays |

## `replace/` — what `replace` writes

Written by hand, **from the rules of `textes/recherche.cas`** — a tag that splits the searched word
encloses it, what the match does not touch does not move — and never read from the program's output.
The input is written by `src/test/e2e/cli/replace_test.cpp`, whose header comment says
why each subtitle is there.

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `replace/bonjour-salut.srt` | the file written by `replace Bonjour Salut`: a tag split the word in subtitle 2, a style follows the match in the 3rd | by hand, rules 2 and 4 of `recherche.cas` |
| `replace/dry-run.txt` | the standard output of `replace --dry-run Bonjour Salut`: subtitles 2 and 3, before and after | by hand: one block per changed subtitle |
| `json/replace-dry-run.jsonl` | the same changes in JSON, with `counts.replaced` and `counts.matched` | by hand |

## `texte/` — what `case`, `italics` and `dialogue-dashes` write

Written by hand, **from the rule corpora of `textes/`** (`casse-titre.cas`, `tirets.cas`…) and the
documentation of `italics`: a tag keeps its case and its place, a leading dash is not touched, an
italic already there is not doubled. The inputs are written by `src/test/e2e/cli/text_rewriting_test.cpp`.

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `texte/casse-titre.srt` | `case --to title` on six texts: an ordinary one, a shouted one, a tag in capitals, a tag that splits a word, two lines, a text already conforming | by hand, rules of `casse-titre.cas` |
| `texte/italiques-on.srt` | `italics --on` on four texts, including a split italic and a text already in italics | by hand |
| `texte/tirets-add.srt` | `dialogue-dashes --add` on five texts, including one already dashed and an opening tag | by hand, rules of `tirets.cas` |
| `json/texte-dry-run.jsonl` | the three subcommands with `--dry-run --format json`: `counts.changed` and `changes` | by hand |

## `sort/` — what `sort` writes

Written by hand: sort the starts, keep ties in the file's order. The inputs are written
by `src/test/e2e/cli/sort_test.cpp`.

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `sort/desordre.srt` | three subtitles, the first of the file starting last | by hand: one, three, five, renumbered |
| `sort/egalite.srt` | two subtitles that start together: the sort is stable | by hand: `a`, then `b-first` before `b-second`, in the file's order |
| `json/sort.jsonl` | a batch of three: disorder (3 places changed), tie (2), already in order (0) | by hand |

## `dry-run/` — the output of `--dry-run`

Compared by `dry_run_test.cpp`, **after replacing the test's temporary directory with
`<scratch>` and the corpus directory with `<corpus>`**, like the JSON expected files. Written by hand.

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `dry-run/narration.txt` | the error output of the six subcommands that write, with `--dry-run` | by hand: each operation's sentence, then `(dry run, nothing written)` in place of `-> <destination>` |
| `dry-run/hearing-impaired.txt` | the standard output of `hearing-impaired --dry-run` on `valides/mentions.srt` | by hand: one block per changed subtitle, `- ` before the old text, `+ ` before the new one, `(removed)` for the emptied subtitle; the dialogue dash of the old text gives `- - ` |

## `translation/` — what a translation file writes

Written by hand, **from the mention-removal rule** (see `mentions.hearing-impaired.srt`) applied
to the translation's text, and never read from the program's output. The input is written by
`src/test/e2e/cli/translation_test.cpp`, laid over the four subtitles of `paires/temoin/principal.srt`.

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `translation/mentions.hearing-impaired.traduction.srt` | the file written by `hearing-impaired --document translation -t`: the first subtitle's mention is its whole text, which is **written empty and keeps the subtitle**; the second's takes the surrounding space with it; the `[1]` reference of the third stays | by hand: four blocks in, four out, **the only writer of the translation being the main document's** — a block without text is read and comes back byte for byte, as `paires/LISEZMOI.md` says |

## `append/` — what `append` writes

Written by hand: the end of the last subtitle of what precedes is the offset of what follows
(four seconds, then five and a half), and the subtitles are renumbered from 1. The inputs
are written by `src/test/e2e/cli/append_test.cpp`.

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `append/deux-fichiers.srt` | two subtitles, then one starting at 0.5 s: it starts at 4.5 s | by hand: 0.5 + 4.0, the italic tag kept |
| `append/trois-fichiers.srt` | the same, then a WebVTT file: it follows the end of the third (5.5 s) | by hand: 1.0 + 5.5 = 6.5 s |
| `json/append.jsonl` | three files, the last in Advanced SSA: the object says what each one cost | by hand: a `{\pos}` tag and the header lost |

## `split/` — what `split-file` writes

Written by hand: the tail is brought back to the origin of the end of the last remaining subtitle (4 s), and
the two halves are renumbered from 1. The input is written by
`src/test/e2e/cli/split_file_test.cpp`: four subtitles, ending at 2, 4, 7 and 9 s, cut at the third.

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `split/coupe-tete.srt` | the first two subtitles, unchanged | by hand |
| `split/coupe-queue.srt` | the last two: 6→2 s, 7→3 s, 8→4 s, 9→5 s | by hand: minus 4 s |
| `json/split-file.jsonl` | the cut at the third: `destination` is the head, `tail` the tail | by hand |

## `pair` — what `pair` writes

**No file of its own**: `pair` writes the translation of each of the eight cases of `paires/`, and its expected files
are **those of that directory** — `attendu-position.traduction.srt` and `attendu-numero.traduction.srt`, written by
hand from the reading of Gaupol before anything aligned anything. `pair_test.cpp` compares them one by one.

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `json/pair.jsonl` | the `temoin` pair: four lines attached, by position | by hand |

## `correct/` — what `correct --dry-run` says

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `correct/dry-run.txt` | the standard output of `correct --tasks mentions,common-errors --dry-run` on `[Door]` and `eﬀet` (the ligature): subtitle 1 removed, the 2nd recomposed — the test's temporary directory is written `<scratch>` in it | by hand: one block per changed subtitle, `- ` before the old text, `+ ` before the new one, no `+` line for a removal |

## `disjoint/` — what `disjoint` writes

Written by hand, **from the rule of issue #698**: cut the timeline at each start and each end of an
overlapping group, merge line by line what is displayed together (earliest first), repeat no
line, leave a gap of under 80 ms to its neighbour, present in windows of two lines what would
have three. The input is `malformes/superpositions.srt`, shaped like a badly merged file: three groups and an
isolated subtitle.

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `disjoint/superpositions.srt` | three overlapping subtitles (the third is in the middle of the first two: three lines, hence two windows), a subtitle that contains another and whose end is bitten by 40 ms (the gap is taken back by the longer neighbour), two subtitles with the same text (a single line, a single subtitle), a subtitle that overlaps nothing | by hand, renumbered |

## `join/` and `repair/` — what `join-repeats` and `repair` write

Written by hand, **from the rule of issue #698**: a same text (same translation and cue settings) cut into
subtitles that follow or overlap one another becomes a single subtitle again, from its smallest start to its greatest end, before
any sorting and any splitting. The input is `malformes/segments-repetes.vtt`, **shaped like a real badly segmented file,
with invented texts**: a text in three chained pieces, and another text, at another position, over the whole range,
given out of order.

| File | Case | Provenance |
| :------ | :-- | :--------- |
| `join/segments-repetes.vtt` | `join-repeats`: the three pieces become one subtitle from 1:47.240 to 1:52.000; the other text is unchanged and the order is the file's | by hand |
| `repair/segments-repetes.vtt` | `repair`: after the merge, nothing to sort, and the two texts that occupy the same range become a two-line subtitle, earliest first, with the first one's settings | by hand |
